title: The Perfect Passive Participle
subtitle: amātus, amāta, amātum. The most useful participle.
objectives: Form the perfect passive participle from the fourth principal part.
Decline it as a first/second declension adjective.
Use it to form perfect passive tenses.

sections.heading: The perfect passive participle
sections.body:
Formation: fourth principal part: amātus, amāta, amātum — loved, having been loved

Declines like bonus, bona, bonum.

Used in perfect passive tenses:
  amātus sum — I have been loved
  captum est — it has been captured

Caesar writes: oppidum captum. — The captured town.
Vergil writes: urbs condita. — The founded city.

items.prompt: Form the perfect participle of dūcō (ductus).
items.answer: ductus, ducta, ductum — led, having been led
The praised girl / the girl who has been praised.
